flawed_step: Exchange step: 'some optimal schedule contains the shortest interval I (swap I for the optimal-schedule intervals it conflicts with without losing size)'. A short interval can conflict with two disjoint intervals of the optimum, one ending inside it and one starting inside it, so the swap loses one interval.
counterexample: Intervals A=[0,5) (len 5), B=[4,7) (len 3), C=[6,12) (len 6), all lengths distinct. A∩B=[4,5)≠∅, B∩C=[6,7)≠∅, A∩C=∅. Greedy picks the unique shortest interval B, which discards A and C, so it returns {B} with size 1 (no ties anywhere). The optimum {A,C} is non-overlapping with size 2. 1 < 2.
assessment_summary: Shortest-duration-first greedy is not optimal for interval scheduling. The exchange argument fails because the shortest interval can overlap two intervals of the optimum. Concrete witness with distinct lengths: [0,5), [4,7), [6,12). Greedy gets 1, optimum gets 2.
